claimed_purpose.text: Evaluates memory and long-dialogue systems across question types covering single-session, multi-session, temporal reasoning, knowledge update, and preference recall.
LongMemEval is used to evaluate end-to-end QA performance of conversational memory systems.

mechanisms.text: The grader dispatches a task-specific LLM-as-judge prompt based on question_type. Five task types are handled: single-session-user, single-session-assistant, multi-session, temporal-reasoning, knowledge-update, and single-session-preference.

The benchmark includes oracle category metadata (dataset-provided category labels) which can be used to select per-category retrieval policies; the issue distinguishes oracle-metadata runs from no-metadata runs as a methodological concern.

LongMemEval-S is a subset/variant of LongMemEval consisting of 500 questions used here for retrieval-only evaluation, where a hit is defined as the gold answer session appearing in the top-k retrieved results.
Each question has a ground truth label that maps to a specific session expected to contain the answer; retrieval systems are evaluated against this session mapping.
For knowledge-update tasks, the judge accepts a response that contains prior information alongside the updated answer, as long as the updated answer is present.
The benchmark uses an official judge prompt applied via an LLM (gpt-4o-2024-08-06) to score system-generated hypothesis answers against gold answers.
Primary metric is overall accuracy (mean of binary correct/incorrect labels across all questions) plus per-question-type accuracy breakdown.
Primary metrics reported are R@5, R@10, and Hit Rate, broken down per category and aggregated overall.
Hypothesis submissions follow a two-field JSONL contract specifying question_id and hypothesis fields.
The judge is invoked via a pipeline script with a top-k parameter.
